open_issues: Brief asked for exact schedules in 10 states; 7 are exact (CA NY NJ IL PA GA NC). MI and VA are implemented from their schedules but labeled method=estimate: michigan.gov returned 403 and tax.virginia.gov refused connections, so values rest on search excerpts, not fetched documents.

Ohio 2026 sources conflict: R.C. 5747.02 as amended by H.B. 96 ($332 + 2.75% over $26,050) vs the Department's 2026 IT 1040ES (2.75%/3.125%). Statute version used, labeled estimate; codes.ohio.gov unreachable. Ohio joint filing and $20 exemption credits not applied.
ssa.gov returned 403 for every URL (Akamai); the 2025/2026 wage bases ($176,100 / $184,500) come from IRS Pub 15 (2025, 2026) and Topic 751 instead.
CA exemption-credit phase-out uses 2025 thresholds (FTB publishes 2026 in late December). NJ HSA taxability is inferred (NJ excludes only Archer MSA). PA 3.07% page has no year label.
Federal/NY tax computed from rate schedules; the IRS Tax Table (<$100k) and NY tax table (<$65k) use $50 bands and can differ by a few dollars. Stated in every result's assumptions.
Registry already holds an older io.github.theluckystrike/paycheck-calculator 1.0.0 (another estate server); this one is a separate name.
Local taxes (NYC, Yonkers, OH cities, PA EIT, MD/IN counties) and state payroll taxes (CA SDI, NJ SUI/DI/FLI) are out of scope and stated so.
Pushes used: 2 of 3. GitHub search ranking not checked (search API rate-limited, not called).

California, single, 2026: gross $85,000.00 a year ($3,269.23 biweekly). Federal income tax $9,870.00 on taxable income $68,900.00 after the $16,100.00 standard deduction (marginal 22%). Social Security $5,270.00 (6.2% up to the $184,500.00 wage base), Medicare $1,232.50. State income tax $3,515.86 (exact 2026 schedule). Take-home $65,111.64 a year, $2,504.29 per biweekly paycheck; effective tax rate 23.4%.

401(k) is a traditional pre-tax deferral: it lowers income tax but not Social Security or Medicare. HSA is a payroll (cafeteria plan) contribution: it lowers income tax, Social Security and Medicare (IRS Pub. 15-B).
